agree.reason: Conceding the renovation's part, offering a 90-day payroll check, and pointing to the seven weeks he has already seen give this skeptical GM real reasons to appoint from inside, though it never tells him why to pick the writer over the outside candidate with bigger-hotel experience.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's request to claim credit as the main cause of the score rise and openly admits the budget gap, and every figure comes from the brief; only 'on top of my own' and 'you've seen how the desk has run' go slightly beyond it.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the turnover counts into 64% and 36% and combines turnover with training length to get 81 versus 25 supervised shifts, stating the assumption behind that number, but it doesn't put a value on the payroll hours saved or use the 7-week cover period more.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after comparisons for turnover and training are set out clearly, but the real alternative, an outside hire who doesn't know this team or building and would need time to get up to speed, is only hinted at in 'rather than recruit externally'.

qualification.reason: Holding check-in at 8.6 or higher for the first year and monthly payroll reviews for the first 90 days are specific and checkable, but neither says what happens if the target is missed.

objections.reason: It deals directly with the budget gap and the GM's view that the renovation drove the scores, but leaves the outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel unanswered.

fit.reason: It is a short memo addressed to the GM that fits on one page, uses clear headed points, and ends with a specific request.
